stories.title: Tunisia's President Saied hosts German FM, calls for 'balance' in EU ties
stories.summary: Tunisia's president Kais Saied welcomed Germany's Foreign Minister to Tunis on Monday for talks on ways to develop their partnership. Saied called on the European Union to update its relationship with Tunisia, saying their partnership should be "more balanced and fair." "Today we spoke about bilateral relations as well as the regional situation," Johann Wadephul, Germany's Foreign Minister, told reporters. "We are living in a time of global upheaval, profound change and crises. The security and economic situation is strained across the world. It is precisely for this reason that international cooperation is now more important than ever. In this regard, I would like to reiterate that Germany and the European Union are, and will remain, reliable friends and partners of Tunisia." The two nations signed financing agreements of almost 100 million euros and pledged to expand cooperation in a number of sectors. "Another pillar of our exchanges is development cooperation, particularly in the areas of the energy transition, water management and digitalisation. I am delighted that we are signing new agreements in the context of this visit. I am convinced that our dialogue and our cooperation will further strengthen cooperation and relations between our countries and our societies."

stories.title: ‘No one else like him’: Argentinians rally for Lionel Messi
stories.summary: Residents of Buenos Aires say they will miss the football legend who won the 2022 World Cup for Argentina. Buenos Aires, Argentina – In the La Boca neighbourhood, home to the Boca Juniors stadium and a place which lives and breathes football, people are taking turns to be photographed in front of huge murals depicting football legend Lionel Messi holding the 2022 World Cup. Across the city, monuments have been illuminated in Argentina’s blue and white in honour of the national hero, who has announced his retirement from international football after two decades during which he was transformed from young prodigy to national icon. On Monday, football clubs around the country were singing songs for Messi and mounting banners showing him holding the World Cup he helped to win for his country. The Argentine Football Association is planning a farewell match to thank him for his extraordinary service. Messi announced his departure from the national team this week on social media with a handwritten letter that he says he wrote two days after losing the World Cup final against Spain this year. He said he had “nothing else to give”. “It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come,” he wrote on Instagram on Monday. While the news has not come as a total surprise – Messi is 39 years old and has recently lost his father, Jorge Messi, who played a crucial role in his career – fans are nevertheless devastated. “We are going to continue loving Messi, not just for football but for his humility, for who he is; that’s the most important thing about Messi,” fan Sebastian Luna tells Al Jazeera. “It’s football; it’s over, but Messi will always be in our hearts”. Some are calling for his number 10 jersey to be retired along with him.

stories.title: European politicians take summer break at inopportune time for Ukraine — Zelensky
stories.summary: Kiev acknowledges that the country has completely exhausted its own resources and that finding funds is becoming increasingly difficult
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.
European allies of Kiev are not addressing issues of assistance to Ukraine because they are on vacation, Vladimir Zelensky said.
"For the past two weeks, Europe and the countries of the world that help us have been on vacation.
And this leaves a bad taste in our mouths.
I really want to sympathize: diplomacy has its schedule.
When it is vacation, it is vacation.
This is a very unpleasant fact," he said in a video published on his Telegram channel.

Earlier, Olga Vasilevskaya-Smaglyuk, a lawmaker from the ruling Servant of the People party, said Ukraine faced a 49.5-billion-euro budget gap, including about 26 billion euros in external funding that Kiev had expected but failed to secure.
Ukraine has drawn up budgets with record deficits for several years.
Kiev acknowledges that the country has completely exhausted its own resources and that finding funds is becoming increasingly difficult.
On August 20, Zelensky admitted that the shortage of funds had become a major challenge, with the defense budget alone facing a $27-billion shortfall.
Former Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmitry Kuleba said that no one in Kiev understands how to fill the budget gap.
